newsitem.title: UK: Amateur rocket breaks sound barrier in UK.
newsitem.headline: Amateur rocket breaks sound barrier in UK.

text.p: The first amateur rocket to break the sound barrier in Europe was launched in Britain on Monday but it was then blown off course and lost.
"It was a complete success. It went over three miles (over 15,000 feet) and broke the sound barrier as we hoped. The rocket stayed together as far as we can tell," rocket-builder Steven Bennett said.
"We haven't got the launch back. We've asked people to keep their eyes peeled and the army are looking for it."
The top third of the rocket was being tested ahead of a complete launch in April. Bennett expects it to reach altitudes of 15 miles (over 17,000 feet).
The world record for an amateur launch is 10 miles.
"We're still on target for April, there was nothing wrong with the motor. This is the run-up to our getting a satellite into space by the new millenium," said Bennett.
The launch of the rocket was arranged by the army at one of their test sites in Northern England.
The upper part is over 10 feet long and the whole rocket will measure 21 feet, said the amateur rocket-builder.
Bennett is currently being sponsored by Lexx, a new science fiction television series due for release later this year.
He is also working with the University of Salford, in Northern England, testing engine power, computer software and parachute mechanisms of the rocket.
Bennett has spent 20 years building some of the world's largest amateur rockets.
